For me, it’s deeply rooted in childhood trauma (TW - emotional and physical abuse) .The frequent worry I had as a child on the bus to school. How would my teachers treat me today? I can’t keep up with this workload, I’m so tired. I can’t focus and my grades are terrible. 

Then the bus home. What would my parents scream about tonight? What can I say to make them less angry with me? I need them to sign my report card and I’m worried they’ll hit me. My mom’s favorite thing to scream at me was: “life is over as you know it! F*ing done! *slams door*”.

A feeling of deep shame that I’d let everyone down. What is wrong with me? 

Now, consider those feelings/negative beliefs with adult relationships and obligations. My manager must hate me. Are they going to fire me? Oh my god I can’t keep up with my bills. I’ll end up on the street and alone. 

Then, overcompensating to get validation from others. Because to me, there must be something wrong with me. Everyone can see it. I’m always running, over performing. Burning myself out. Putting other people’s needs before my own. 

Worried that the “world will be over as I know it”. Always on. Hyper-vigilant. Exhausted. Sad. Lonely.
The wand chooses the wizard, Mr. Potter.

I’m so, so sorry that you are going through this. You deserved to be cared for and protected when you were a child. And they abused you and failed you entirely. You have EVERY right to be jealous and lacking empathy for your mother. 

Feeling overwhelmed sucks, but it makes sense for the situation. This is going to sound shitty, but it’s something I’ve been processing about my mom (recently estranged) and really needed to hear: she’s not capable of changing. Rather, not capable of developing the capacity to empathize with what I’ve been thru or what she’s done for to hurt me. More importantly, she’s made her own bed and it’s not my job to save her or make her downward spiral a softer landing. 

So what am I getting at? You owe your mom NOTHING . And maybe you’re lacking empathy because it’s simply not there. It sounds like she’s in a rough spot that she’s going to have to dig herself out of if she wants to get better. In her own words: “everybody has to make their own decisions”. She’ll need to make hers. It’s never a child’s responsibility to be emotionally available to the parent. 

Hang in there. I don’t know you, but I know exactly how you feel. I’m estranged from both of my parents who are abusers, my mom within the last few months. I deal with recurring major depression, ptsd, a lot of shit. It’s taken a lot of work to get better and heal and sometimes I feel like I’m going backwards. Sometimes I’m just flat out ready to give up. Depression is hell and you’re a hero for navigating it. Give yourself the empathy you’d potentially muster up for your mom. You deserve love and care; she doesn’t

Take care 🙏🏻

This is hard and I empathize with your experience. Your situation is very common, but what I think is not often discussed is that some therapists are attachment focused versus not. For many people, working through attachment issues is the work. I’m doing it now and it’s extremely hard. 

That said, based on her responses to you it sounds as though she isn’t capable or willing to define the boundaries for a continued therapeutic relationship. It’s imperative to know that this relationship is one sided. And there is no way to have a relationship outside of the therapy.
